sentences.text: Yamanasaurus possessed a stocky, quadrupedal body featuring an elongated neck and tail, reaching an estimated length of approximately 6 meters.
Like other saltasaurines, this dinosaur likely bore protective armor composed of osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin.
This species represents the first non-avian dinosaur formally described from Ecuador.
Evidence suggests it fed on low vegetation, indicating a browsing lifestyle.
The holotype, which is the specific specimen the species is based on, was discovered in 2017 when an octogenarian resident named Francisco Celi found a vertebra.
Celi subsequently informed professor Galo Guamán and his students about the find.
Yamanasaurus lojaensis is the type and only species within its genus.
It belongs to the family Saltasauridae and the parent group Saltasaurinae.
Taxonomically, the animal is classified within the class Saurischia.
Fossils indicate Yamanasaurus lived in Ecuador during the Campanian-Maastrichtian stages of the late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 70 million years ago.
Professor Galo Guamán determined the fossil age through geological correlation, suggesting the animal existed during the Maastrichtian period, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
